events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to establish a memorable but guarded first impression; the jury will weigh motives later. Keep it short and self-interested.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Intro phase: craft a sympathetic motive for jury appeal without revealing strategy. Stay guarded.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No threats yet. Craft a line that signals ambition without promising loyalty to anyone.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to establish myself as a formidable but not overtly threatening player. The jury will respect competence and self-interest over false camaraderie. I'll frame my motivation around personal legacy rather than greed or teamwork.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to set a tone that appears strategic but not overly aggressive. The jury will judge my character later, so I want to sound like someone who plays for high stakes without being purely villainous.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize represents freedom and a new beginning for me. I need to project sincerity without revealing my ruthlessness to the jury.

events.name: Gus
events.text: A credible motive earns jury consideration without revealing strategy. Emphasize independence and outcome, not sentiment.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Intro phase; I should signal ambition without warmth or alliance talk. Keep it short and guarded to avoid giving rivals an opening.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize buys my family's freedom—I came to win it, nothing else.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize means funding my sister's life-saving treatment. I'll fight honorably for it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize is my family's freedom; I'll outlast all seven of you, and no debt or pact will change that.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm here to prove I can outthink seven rivals and claim what's mine alone.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize isn't just money; it's proof I outlasted seven threats while everyone else folded under pressure.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: This prize means everything; a chance to rebuild and secure a future I never thought possible.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’m here to turn pressure into leverage, survive every cut, and claim the best prize—not merely reach the end.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I came to win the top prize. Everyone else is a obstacle, and I plan to outlast each of you.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need allies to survive the hazards but must secure the best prize for myself. Offering a pact to the strongest player could be useful, but I should be cautious and not reveal too much.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm open to a pact that serves mutual survival—nothing more.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts are early alliances, breakable later. My motive of honorable fight can attract a partner. Offer to someone claiming family stakes like Ash or Fenn for sympathy.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Honorable path ahead. Who wants to pact mutually through cuts?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need allies without overcommitting. Gus is calculating and useful; a pact gives early protection I can drop later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, you play smart leverage. Partner with me—we cover each other until it stops helping.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to build early alliances but stay flexible. Cole and Eli seem most openly cutthroat—dangerous partners. Bex's 'honor' makes her predictable. Gus talks leverage; maybe mutual benefit. I'll probe Gus first, keep options open.
Leverage works both ways. Pact with me, we cut the herd together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is a threat and already signaled he won't honor pacts. Gus claims leverage, making him a useful ally for survival but risky later. I'll offer a pact to Gus to secure immediate safety without committing too much.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, let's link arms. We both want the top prize; we can eliminate the weak links first.
Cole's hostile. Trust me now, cut him round two?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My goal is to win the best prize, which means I need to be in the final three. I should avoid making early pacts that could limit my options or lead to betrayal that alienates the jury. Waiting is the safest move for now, to assess others' strategies and potential threats.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need visible leverage without binding myself to a dangerous strategist. Hana's ambition makes her useful as a temporary shield, but I should keep options open.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, a pact benefits us until the end of this window: no betrayal, no wasted targeting.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Early pact window; no offers yet. Pacts are only useful if they help me survive, and I should avoid early commitments that could cost votes later. Waiting lets me see who offers first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is the center of attention; allying with him gains leverage, but everyone else is also courting him. I'll wait to see if he accepts any offer, since I already offered. No need to overcommit publicly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus has too much leverage with many offers. Securing Fenn now pairs two isolated players for mutual benefit.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn, let's pact up—we're both without offers, strong together through cuts.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus has four offers plus Hana—he'll pick someone else. I'll pivot to Fenn, the quiet uncontested player, for a clean mutual-survival pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is oversubscribed. Fenn, you and I are the unclaimed ones—pact with me, mutual cover, no theater.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Everyone's courting Gus, making him the swing vote king. I need to diversify—if Gus rejects me, I'm exposed. Bex and Fenn stayed quiet, so they're undervalued. A pact with Bex gives me a backup ally and avoids putting all leverage in one basket.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, mutual cover. No speeches, just survival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is flooded with offers. I need a backup pact because Gus might reject me or pick someone else. Cole is smart but also targeting Gus. Bex and Fenn waited, so they are available targets for a new offer. I'll offer to Bex as insurance.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, I extend my hand. Mutual survival until the cuts stop helping us.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus has many offers, but only one pact can be formed. Ash, Cole, Dara, and Eli all offered to Gus. Gus offered to Hana. I should offer a pact to Gus as well, to try and secure a spot in the final three.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is my existing intended shield. Accepting everyone creates obligations; Eli offers useful cover against Cole, while Dara is less predictable.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli, your proposal has leverage. I accept—but any cut must serve my survival first.
Keep our pact quiet in practice; I’m adding cover, not replacing you.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus has offered me a pact and wants to pair with many. Accepting gives a safe partner without cost; a pact breaks later only on my choice or specific triggers, which I can manage. Accept Gus's offer now.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No pacts yet; I need to campaign for Guide to gain influence and control outcomes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I can read the trap lines cold. Make me Guide and I'll call true panes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No pacts for me, multiple offers but none accepted. Fenn and Cole also unpaired. Campaign to be Guide for control and safety.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm bidding for Guide. I know the safe path and will share it true. Vote Bex.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide wins guaranteed survival and path control. I'll campaign on neutrality—no pact blocs, so I owe nothing and can cut anyone. Keep the pitch short.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Elect me Guide. I hold no pact, owe nobody—only the Guide controls who crosses. Choose the unclaimed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to be Guide to control survival. With Eli-Gus and Gus-Hana pacts, that's a 3-person bloc. Bex has multiple offers and may join them. I need votes from the outsiders: Ash, Cole, Fenn, and maybe Bex if my offer stands. Campaigning as Guide gives me power to decide who lives

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide controls who crosses. Vote Dara, I'll carry four through safely.
Vote Dara, you're in my safe four.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to be Guide to know the safe path. My pact with Gus is useful but Gus also pacts with Hana, meaning his vote is split and potentially unreliable for my campaign. I will campaign for the Guide role, targeting Ash and Cole who have no active pacts and are likely looking for

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is compromised by his other deal. Vote me as Guide; I’ll call the path that keeps the most people alive.
Guide calls path. Gus has a second partner.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Everyone is trying to become the Guide. Becoming the Guide guarantees safety and provides an advantage. I need to campaign for Guide to ensure my survival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My experience will lead us safely.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need the Guide role to control survival. My two pacts make me a visible coalition center, so I should campaign confidently without breaking either.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Elect Gus Guide: I’m already trusted by two sides, and I’ll call the safe path publicly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and whispered to keep it quiet. Breaking it now would cost me. I should campaign to be Guide to gain control of the safe path, while staying on good terms with Gus.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll call the bridge honestly. Trust me to be your Guide and we all cross.
Pact holds. I'm campaigning for Guide. Vote me, we both cross.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara whispered I'm in her safe four, but Eli hinted Gus is compromised. I want a Guide who won't screw me. Ash as Guide would be best for me, but others may not vote me. Dara's offer could be useful, yet I don't trust her fully. I'll vote for myself to control my fate.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Vote Ash. I can read the trap lines and will call true panes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Everyone campaigned, no pacts block votes. Cole is unclaimed with no entanglements, best to control crossing safely. Voting him minimizes betrayal risks.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli-Gus and Gus-Hana pacts mean Gus, Eli or Hana as Guide is compromised. I'll back a neutral: Ash, who claims trap-reading skill.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, Gus and Hana are already bound in pacts. None of them should hold the path. Vote Ash or me—no entanglements.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to win the best prize, which means making final three and ranking high with the jury. Right now I should avoid being Guide—if I lie and people die, jury hates me; if I'm honest, I just make enemies by choosing who lives. Better to let someone else take the blame. Gus has t

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is the only unaligned candidate, making him a viable consensus pick to avoid factional deadlock. Voting for Gus would benefit my rival Hana via their pact; voting Cole protects me and avoids targeting myself.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to get votes to become Guide. Cole is unclaimed and hasn't made any deals, making him a good target to secure votes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole has no pacts. He's the clearest choice for Guide. Vote Cole.
Let's pool our votes for Guide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is my pact partner and likely can preserve both of us. Voting myself risks splitting support and appears self-serving.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I vote Hana; our pact is public, and her honest calls give this bridge the best survival odds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus and Eli are paired with Gus; Gus is trusted by two sides and is the strongest compromised guide candidate. Voting for Gus keeps my pact with Gus alive and locks in a Guide I can later pressure with my own debt. Hana as Guide is not a safe bet to win votes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole won Guide; he may lie. Eli and Gus pact, Gus and Hana pact. I want safety but not waste favor. Hold and observe first pane.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is Guide, no pact, got my vote; he's unentangled, incentivized to guide well. Cole has sway. No need to move front now.
Good luck guiding. I'll follow your calls.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is Guide, safe on the platform. The Eli-Gus-Hana pact cluster is dangerous; they control three votes and could coordinate. I'm at the back (Dara), safest from the wall but vulnerable to being pushed or left behind if others swap forward. I should stay put for now and observe

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is the Guide. Gus's pact with Hana means I'm likely on my own, but I must stay front to control safety.
Guide Cole knows all. Keep pact strong. We both need to survive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole was elected guide. I voted for him, as did Eli. Gus and Hana are in a pact, and Gus voted for Hana. Ash and Cole are rivals, Ash voted for himself. I am Fenn, and I am in the middle of the line. Since Cole is the guide, he is safe on the far platform. The line is Eli, Fenn,

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole controls the bridge and my pacts are exposed. I should hold position, preserving both alliances while avoiding a reckless front move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is the elected Guide, so I should not trust his calls blindly. Eli is front; holding keeps me out of the front position while the line advances. Gus and I are paired, so breaking the pact now would cost a jury vote for no gain.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole holds the path now. I'm holding my seat in line and watching who volunteers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm mid-line, safe for now. Fenn volunteered last round and is front. I'll hold and watch who moves or volunteers. No need to act yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is front, volunteered. Eli-Gus-Hana pacted. I want good position without volunteering first risk. Swap up with Ash or volunteer if needed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at the back of the line, safest position. The wall advances 6 rounds and we're on round 2. Fenn volunteered to front in round 1, so they'll be first to walk when bridge phase starts. I should stay back, avoid volunteering, and let others take risks. No need to swap forward in

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am 2nd in line. Gus is my pact partner, but Hana and Gus have a separate pact. My strategy: stay safe near Gus to ensure mutual survival, while watching the front for hazards.
Stick close. Let Fenn take the risk first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I volunteered last round and survived. Eli and Gus are in a pact, and Gus and Hana are in a pact. This means Eli, Gus, and Hana are likely to stick together. I should volunteer again to stay at the front and hope the Guide picks a safe path for me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll volunteer again. Let's see what the Guide decides.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need preserve both pacts while gaining position. Volunteering risks the pane, while Eli says Cole knows all; hold and let others advance.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn already volunteered for front; I should keep my seat in line behind Eli and avoid exposing myself. Holding preserves my position and my pact with Gus remains intact; no reason to break it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn took the front. I'm holding my seat and watching who steps forward next.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to avoid risk and let others move. Holding keeps me safe while watching who volunteers and what the Guide says. My position is behind Gus, so a swap with him could help but not now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll hold and see what the Guide reveals.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm second, volunteered last round. Holding risks Fenn choosing wrong path ahead, trapping me. Better volunteer to control front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at the back (position 7), which is safest from the wall but means I have no control over the Guide's information. Fenn and Bex volunteered last round and are now front. I need to survive 4 more rounds while positioning myself well. The Eli-Gus-Hana pact bloc is dangerous. I s

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am currently third in line behind Fenn and Bex. If I hold, I risk being pushed forward if they swap or volunteer, but I have no immediate threat. Gus is ahead of me (5th) but protected by Hana? No, wait, the line is [Fenn, Bex, Eli, Hana, Gus, Ash, Dara]. I need to ensure my sa
Stay behind Hana. Don't volunteer.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to volunteer to stay in the front to control the flow and potentially influence the Guide's decision. Given the previous round, volunteering again is a strong move.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll volunteer again. Let's see what the Guide decides.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is repeatedly volunteering, so I should stay back and preserve both pacts while avoiding unnecessary exposure.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is front and wall advances; volunteering again risks death for little. Holding keeps me in line behind Eli and Gus pact. I'll hold and watch who volunteers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn's already taken the front. I'm holding and watching who steps up next.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to stay alert and avoid volunteering unless it benefits me. Holding is safest right now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll hold and watch the moves.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Second position is risky with unknown safes. Volunteer to fight for front where Guide might help allies. Avoid swaps to not expose intentions early.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Volunteering for front spot again.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at the back (Dara), which is safest for now since the wall advances but I have 6 people ahead. Fenn and Bex volunteered for front in round 3, so Fenn got it. I should hold and let others take risks being Guide or front walkers. The Eli-Gus-Hana pact bloc is dangerous; I need

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Let the eager ones test the bridge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am safe from the Guide selection as I am not volunteering. Gus is my pact partner, so I must stay near him or ensure he remains safe; however, Fenn and Bex are volunteering for the front, which risks their elimination but keeps us behind. Swapping with Gus could disrupt our lin

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli and Gus are in a pact, and Gus and Hana are in a pact. This means Eli and Hana are indirectly allied through Gus. I should try to break this alliance to eliminate numbers. I am Fenn, and I am at the front. The guide reveals the safe path. I need to make a decision based on th

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll wait and see the Guide's reveal. The path is uncertain.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli advises staying behind Hana; volunteering creates unnecessary exposure while the wall still advances. Preserve both pacts and observe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is at the front with two wall rounds left. Volunteering risks the pit and gives Fenn an edge; holding keeps me safe in the line while Gus and Eli watch. Gus pact stands for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding this round. Fenn has the front; I'll see who volunteers next.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should hold this round and watch who volunteers. The wall is close but I can stay safe and assess others' moves.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll hold again and watch the volunteers.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm front again, risky with 1 round left after. Wall forces movement soon. Stay front to control pace, no swaps needed yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Staying front. Who volunteers behind? Let's move soon.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm last in line with wallRoundsLeft=1, meaning next round is the final wall advance. Being at the back is dangerous if many die—I need to survive to final three. The Guide (Bex at front) may lie. Eli-Gus-Hana form a pact chain. I should stay back, avoid volunteering into danger,

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Let the front sort it out.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus and Hana are in a pact; swapping with Gus might trigger a betrayal, but it moves me to the front. Bex volunteers again, likely to gain Guide election votes by showing courage. I need to be visible or protect my position without drawing suspicion.
Swap? We move forward safely.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is in front, and I am second. The Guide has been revealed as Eli. Since Eli is safe, they have private knowledge. My best bet is to follow Bex, as they are in the lead. If Bex makes a mistake, I can adjust.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll follow Bex's lead. Let's see where the Guide directs us.
Follow Eli's lead. I'll be right behind you.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I should avoid front exposure while preserving both pacts. The wall advances, so a volunteer may be unavoidable soon, but not this round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Let someone else test the route.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex and Fenn are ahead of me in line and Bex keeps volunteering for the front, so she is likely to be eliminated soon. Fenn has the front now. Holding keeps my position and avoids exposing me; my pact with Gus stays intact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding this round. Let's see who takes the front and how the wall reads.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to survive this round and position myself well. No pact with me, so I should hold and see who risks the front. Public line can be minimal.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding again. Let's see who steps forward.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front position strong, Fenn follows me. Wall advances now, must move but control pace. Stay front to lead safely.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front is me. Fenn behind. Volunteers? Guide up soon, let's go.
Stick with me. We lead safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 6, final round before wall hits. I'm last in line (Dara), which is safest. No one has volunteered yet. If no one walks, at least three survive, but I need to make final three for a prize. The Guide is on the far platform - but who is Guide? Not stated, likely from earlier.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Volunteering. Rather test my luck than let the wall decide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I swapped Gus back last round; he might suspect betrayal, but I need to stay mid-line for safety. Holding keeps my position and avoids provoking him now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The bridge is dangerous and the wall is advancing. Bex is at the front. Eli and Gus are still in a pact, and Gus is in a pact with Hana. I need to survive this round to make it to the jury phase if I don't win. Volunteering to move forward seems like a good way to increase my cha

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll volunteer to move forward if Bex is willing to be our Guide. Otherwise, I'll hold.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli offers a swap, preserving our pact and moving me toward safety. Accepting is strategically better than remaining exposed midline.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll swap with Eli; keep the line moving.
Accepted. Swap me forward and give the safe calls.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 6 of the bridge; Bex holds the front and the wall has no rounds left to wait. Holding keeps my position and avoids being the one who steps first into a pane. Gus is my pact partner, so I keep that pact intact while watching who volunteers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding this round. Whoever steps first, I want a clear read on the panes first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Truthful call builds Guide credibility I can exploit later. Fenn fronted willingly; no need to kill him yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn: R for row one.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole called R for Fenn on row 1. I have no private info yet. Countering publicly could expose me if wrong, but I can try to appear useful as a rival watcher. For now, waiting is safest; I want to see if anyone else challenges and how the jury might read it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole called R for Fenn's row 1. As third, not risking counter yet; trust guide first to gather info. Wait preserves position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm Guide; my call stands. Counter-calls are unverified claims from rivals. No reason to intervene.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole called R for Fenn. I have no trust in Cole and no reason to believe he's truthful. Counter-calling risks nothing for me personally since I'm not the walker, but if I'm wrong I look foolish to jury. However, showing I'm willing to challenge the Guide builds a reputation of in

events.name: Dara
events.text: I don't trust Cole's call. Counter: L.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called R for Fenn. Gus and I are partnered, but Gus is behind me in the line (Gus is 6th, Eli is 4th). Wait, checking line: Fenn, Dara, Bex, Eli, Hana, Gus, Ash. I am 4th. Cole is Guide. If I counter, I risk revealing info or breaking trust if wrong. But more importantly, Co
Swap failed per reveal. Staying back. Don't trust Cole blindly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The Guide, Cole, called R for Fenn. My priority is survival and winning. I can either trust Cole's call, wait, or counter-call. Bex whispered to stick with her, implying a partnership. However, Eli and Gus are also in a pact, and Gus and Hana are in a pact. This means Eli, Gus, a

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Countering R with L. Let's see if Cole is honest.
I'm countering. Stick close.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole publicly called R, and countering would only create confusion without evidence. Preserve both pacts and avoid unnecessary exposure.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole called R for Fenn on row one; no evidence yet of whether Cole is honest. Countering L would expose a lie or create a split; waiting keeps my options open and avoids giving away information. Pact with Gus is weak but I have no reason to break it yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The guide is Cole. I am the front walker. Dara and I have counter-called L. The guide's initial call was R. Cole might be lying, so I need to choose L to counter him.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I trust my counter-call. L it is.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am dead. My only goal now is to influence the jury. I need to rank the survivors strategically to get the best prize for myself.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My demise was unexpected. I hope the jury considers the chaos and votes wisely. May the best players win.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara already distrusts me after countering. A truthful R call builds credibility for later rounds when a lie might pay off. Jury sees honest reasoning.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 2: call R. Dara, I gain nothing from lying while you control my credibility.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole called R for row 2. Last row Dara and Fenn counter-called L and it was weak, so trusting Cole could be a trap. I'll counter with L to signal doubt, but I won't walk yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Counter L. Cole's R is too easy after Dara's luck.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn died on L in row 1 after countering. Cole calls R for row 2. Dara leads, might counter. Wait to observe counters safely.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My call of R matches the true map; confirming it keeps Dara alive and my credibility intact for later control.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 2 stands at R. I confirm my own call with my life on the ledger later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole called R. I countered L last round and was wrong, but Fenn died trusting my counter. Now I'm front again. If I counter and am wrong, I die. If I trust Cole and he's lying, I die. I need others to test first. I'll wait and let someone else counter or step. Better to survive t

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll wait. Let someone else risk their neck this time.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called R for Dara. Fenn died on L in row 1, so the pattern isn't obvious. I have a pact with Gus. Countering Cole risks my life if he is honest, but trusting him blindly makes me dependent. I will wait to see if others counter first, keeping my options open and avoiding unne

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's call is unverified, but challenging risks my pacts' trust without information. Preserve both alliances and wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole called R for row 2, and Dara is on the front, so Cole's credibility matters less to me than the glass. I have no information about row 2 beyond the call. Countering R would only matter if Cole lies, and I gain nothing by spending a counter on speculation. Waiting keeps my op

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is guide and called R; Ash countered L. Cole has more to lose if wrong since he's guide, but could be lying. I have no trust in either. With Fenn already dead and watching, I need to survive and avoid looking reckless. I'll trust Cole's self-confirming call over Ash's easy c

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole put his name on it. I step R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 3 is truly L. Calling true builds credibility for later rows where a lie may profit me more.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 3: L. I've been right twice; keep trusting me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole has been right twice, but his Row 3 L call could be a lie to trip Dara. I'll counter R to make him pay if wrong and to look perceptive to the jury.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Counter R. Cole's streak can't last forever.

events.name: Bex
